definition: Logit adjustments that discourage tokens already generated, suppressing loops and verbatim repetition.
details: Logit adjustments that discourage tokens already generated, suppressing loops and verbatim repetition. Blunt instruments: overuse degrades text that legitimately needs repetition (code, names).

explainer.lead: Presence penalties adjust logits to discourage tokens already generated, suppressing loops and verbatim repetition. They matter because degenerate repetition is a common failure in long generations.

tiers.eli5: If you already said a word, the tool gives it a small nudge down so you don't keep saying it over and over.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers raise the penalty when outputs loop, but it is a blunt instrument. The pitfall is overuse degrading text that legitimately needs repetition, such as code and names.
tiers.paperLevel: Presence penalties are logit adjustments that discourage tokens already generated, suppressing loops and verbatim repetition; being blunt, overuse harms outputs that legitimately require repetition.

explainer.example: With a moderate presence penalty, a model stops repeating the same sentence verbatim in a long essay, while a high penalty mangles repeated variable names in code.
